contract.goal: starters a service uses to configure microservice-to-microservice communication over gRPC, with the platform's cross-cutting contracts carried across the transport
contract.output: grpc-core + grpc-server-spring-boot-starter + grpc-client-spring-boot-starter, protobuf build support in ludwig-bom and the root POM, scripts/check_protos.sh in the gate, RuleGroup.GRPC in architecture-rules, READMEs in both locales
constraints: no existing call site, REST endpoint or @LudwigRestClient is migrated or changed
no second problem registry, audit sink, operation vocabulary, cache primitive or preference type
no rule is weakened, no test disabled, to make progress
done_when: scripts/manifest.sh build && scripts/manifest.sh stale && scripts/manifest.sh layout

decisions: 1.1: grpc-java 1.84.2 (current stable on Maven Central, 2026-10-11) and protobuf-java 3.25.9, because that is the protobuf version grpc-protobuf 1.84.2 declares; protobuf 4.x is NOT used although newer, since the design ties the runtime to what grpc-protobuf was built against
1.2: io.github.ascopes:protobuf-maven-plugin 5.1.11 (requires Java 17 and Maven 3.9.6, both met)
add-sonarcloud-analysis was committed as 0a68e84 before this change started, so the prerequisite in tasks.md group 1 is met

1.2 finding: the root POM cannot read ludwig-bom's properties (a BOM import does not reach plugin configuration; lombok.version is the existing precedent), so protoc.version and protoc-gen-grpc-java.version repeat the BOM's protobuf.version and grpc.version in the root POM. The pom-topology delta said 'no second edit'; the code is the truth, so the delta scenario was rewritten to 'the gate fails when a pair differs' and scripts/check_protos.sh gained E_GENERATOR_DRIFT to enforce it

1.3: one JaCoCo exclusion pattern (**/grpc/v*/**) instead of the two in tasks.md, because grpc-core's own proto follows the contract convention (java_package ru.ludwigandreas.operation.grpc.v1) rather than a private ru.ludwigandreas.grpc.core.proto package; Sonar exclusion is **/generated-sources/protobuf/** (the plugin's output directory) so QueryDSL/MapStruct analysis is unchanged
2.1: check_protos.sh lists untracked files too (git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard), unlike check_migrations.sh - a new contract is first checked before it is ever added

2.4: architecture-rules fixtures use same-FQN test stubs for io.grpc.*, the stereotype, PreAuthorize and ProtocolMessageEnum, the existing convention in that module's test tree; the rule set also forbids @Cacheable/@Async/@PermitAll/@DenyAll/@PreFilter/@PostFilter on a gRPC service, which share the same proxy defect
2.5: prefix stripping in OperationVocabularyRules applies only to enums implementing com.google.protobuf.ProtocolMessageEnum, so hand-written Java enums are judged exactly as before

baseline: the full reactor build logs 'Unsupported class file major version 70' from JaCoCo 3148 times before any change here (Maven runs on a newer JDK than JaCoCo 0.8.12 instruments); it is pre-existing noise, not a failure, and is not addressed by this change

3.3: the status table is a switch expression with no default over ProblemStatus (and over OperationStatus in 3.4), so a status added to web-core fails grpc-core's COMPILATION, which is stronger than the unit test the task asked for; the test is kept as well

3.3: free-form problem properties (including web-core's optional 'debug' member) are deliberately not forwarded in the gRPC status; only code, http status, type, title, detail, violations, retry-after and correlation id travel

3.5: the bridge is a static helper (ContextRestoringServerInterceptor.interceptCall/within) plus the ThreadBinding SPI, not an interceptor class - what goes INTO the context differs per concern and lives in the server starter

4.1: grpc-inprocess is an OPTIONAL compile dependency of the server starter, not test scope as tasks.md says: the published @LudwigGrpcServerTest slice (main code) builds the in-process server and channel. spring-boot-test, spring-boot-test-autoconfigure, spring-test and junit-jupiter-api are optional for the same reason, as in rest-client

4.3: the fixed chain is the declaration order of BuiltInServerInterceptor.Stage (OBSERVATION, CORRELATION, ACCESS_LOG, EXCEPTION, ADMISSION, AUTHENTICATION, CONTEXT, REPLAY). Two refinements of design D5, neither reordering it: the correlation id is RESOLVED into the gRPC Context at its own stage near the top (so the access log and a refused call's rendered problem carry it) and only BOUND to the MDC by the context bridge; and saturation is refused at an ADMISSION stage inside the exception translator, so the refusal is rendered through the problem pipeline and costs no token validation

4.3: the exception translator renders inside the context the bridge built (handed outwards through a per-call CallState in the gRPC Context), because by the time an outer stage holds the failure the bridge's bindings are undone and the problem would be rendered in the JVM locale. A failure raised before the bridge (authentication, admission) is rendered in the platform default locale

4.4: AuthenticationInterceptor is absent, not no-op, when there is no JwtDecoder bean; the validator fails startup on an absent AUTHENTICATION stage unless security.enabled=false. Identity metadata stripped is security-starter's SecurityHeaders.CLIENT_FORBIDDEN (all of it, XFCC included: there is no trusted-proxy notion on the gRPC port); with security-starter absent the list is empty
4.5: UserPreferences are resolved once per call on the first callback (principal already bound) and memoised in the call's Context, rather than resolved on every callback

4.6: server TLS is configured by naming a Spring Boot SSL bundle (ludwig.grpc.server.tls.bundle + client-auth), not by the truststore/keystore/protocols keys design D14 sketches - one place for key material, shared with the HTTP port. ludwig.grpc.allow-plaintext and ludwig.grpc.production-profiles are read from the Environment because they belong to neither starter. No bundle means plaintext, which is accepted on a loopback address or with both switches, and never under a production profile (loopback included)

4.10 finding: rest-client's @LudwigRestClientTest.include() maps to 'spring.test.importautoconfiguration.include', a property nothing in Spring Boot reads, so it has no effect. Not fixed (rest-client must not be modified by this change); @LudwigGrpcServerTest has no include attribute and a test adds auto-configurations with @ImportAutoConfiguration

4.8: idempotent replay reuses IdempotencyStore, RequestFingerprint.ofPayload, IdempotencyProperties.ttlFor/leaseFor, IdempotencyMetrics and the idempotency module's own exceptions; @Idempotent is read on the handler METHOD only (a class-level annotation would opt in streaming methods). The claim is settled at close(OK) so asynchronous handlers are covered; a handler that throws releases the key from inside the stage, because the translator closes the call from outside it. Not done, unlike IdempotencyFilter: audit records for replay/mismatch, and the max-stored-response cap (gRPC message size limits bound it instead)

4.9: observation is Micrometer's ObservationGrpcServerInterceptor with a convention renamed to ludwig.grpcserver.requests{service,method,status}, fed ObservationRegistry.NOOP when the application has none; the access log is one INFO line per call on ludwig.grpcserver.<service> with method, status, duration and correlation id

4.10: package structure changed to satisfy cycles.modules-are-free-of-cycles: GrpcServerProperties -> .properties (registered as a configuration package in architecture-rules.properties, as odata-filter does), GrpcServerMessages and GrpcServerConfigurationException -> .error, the validator -> .server, the slice's auto-configuration -> .config; GrpcServerLifecycle no longer depends on the interceptor package (the config passes whether an AUTHENTICATION stage exists). GrpcServerProperties is @Validated (port, executor.threads, executor.queue-capacity, max-concurrent-calls-per-connection) and the validator's own executor-bounds check was removed in favour of it. Two rules are disabled in the module's ArchitectureTest with the reason in its javadoc: tests.production-code-does-not-depend-on-test-frameworks (the published slice) and exceptions.custom-exceptions-extend-the-base-exception (the startup refusal is not a rendered problem)

5.x: a typed client failure is the CAUSE of the StatusRuntimeException a generated stub throws, not the thrown type - a generated stub's exception type cannot be changed from an interceptor. GrpcClientException.from(e) reads it, and web-core's ProblemMapperRegistry already walks the cause chain, so GrpcClientProblemMapper renders it with no advice. This refines design D11's 'failures surface as one hierarchy'

5.3: stub and named-channel injection is a BeanDefinitionRegistryPostProcessor (GrpcClientBeanRegistrar) that finds @LudwigGrpcClient injection points - fields, constructor and method parameters, @Bean method parameters and the fields of the type a @Bean method returns - before any bean exists, registers one stub bean per (client, stub type) with a LudwigGrpcClient qualifier, and fails startup naming the injection point for an unknown client. @LudwigGrpcClient is meta-annotated @Qualifier and @Autowired. Channel beans are '<name>GrpcChannel', qualified both @Qualifier(name) and @LudwigGrpcClient(name)

5.6: the retryable methods are found by scanning ru.ludwigandreas for generated <Service>Grpc classes (the package check_protos.sh enforces) and reading each method's idempotency_level from its proto descriptor; one method list serves every client because a full method name is unique, and only the policy differs per client. Scanning, rather than collecting from stub injection points, is what makes the channel and registry models retry identically to an injected stub, since a channel is built before any stub is known

5.5: Resilience4j instances are named grpc-<client> in the application's registries (ofDefaults when it has none), so a rest-client client and a gRPC client of the same name never share a breaker. Bulkhead uses acquirePermission (honours max-wait); the breaker releases the permit unrecorded for caller-side codes and UNAUTHENTICATED

5.7: credentials are CallCredentials applied per attempt on gRPC's executor; relay captures the caller's token on the caller's thread into a CallOptions key, and with no token the credentials fail the attempt before anything is sent. A provider-defined type is any auth.type a GrpcCallCredentialsProvider bean answers to; 'custom' is not a reserved word. The UNAUTHENTICATED re-attempt is an interceptor replaying the buffered unary request once with FORCE_REFRESH, holding the first attempt's response headers back

5.x tests: the client ITs run against a hand-built, scriptable in-process server (ScriptedServer) instead of the server starter the migration plan mentions - the client's own failure modes (fail N times, pushback, pause, observe deadline and credential) need a peer the test controls, and the server starter is already proven by its own suite. Balancing is proven with three Netty servers behind a test NameResolver

5.11: refresh mirrors rest-client: ClientRuntime re-merges the bound properties at most once a second; deadline, logging level, audit sampling and the rate limiter's limit-for-period (changeLimitForPeriod) are read per call at its start, so a call in flight keeps its policy. In-process targets get no load-balancing policy (a direct address refuses one)
6.x: README module table rows, the CLAUDE.md bullet and the openspec/config.yaml context bullet added; the commented grpc-client placeholder row removed

8.1: GrpcCallContext.INBOUND_BEARER_TOKEN (grpc-core) carries the caller's raw token beside the authentication; the server's authentication stage sets it; the client's relay reads it before the security context. GrpcServerToClientIT runs both starters in one application with LudwigAuthentication as the principal and asserts the downstream call carries the caller's token, a deadline within the inbound one and the inbound correlation id. grpc-server-spring-boot-starter and test-support-security are test-scope dependencies of the client starter
